title: SpaceX wins FCC approval to deploy 1 million orbital data center satellites
summary: SpaceX won approval from the FCC to put 1 million orbital data center satellites into space, a proposal that was opposed by Amazon and other groups.
body: The Federal Communications Commission has authorized Elon Musk 's SpaceX to put 1 million artificial intelligence computing satellites in orbit, Chairman Brendan Carr announced on Wednesday. Carr said in a post on X, the social network owned by SpaceX, that the company's Starmind constellation, and "competitor constellations will use solar power to extend America's lead" in AI. Musk said in a reply, "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world." The FCC, in its authorization filing , noted that SpaceX's application "received a substantial number of comments from the public, including petitions to deny filed by Kuiper Systems LLC ( Amazon Leo), Viasat Inc. (Viasat), and the American Astronomical Society (AAS)." In a March petition urging the FCC to deny SpaceX's application, Amazon had labeled the company's Starmind project as a "lofty ambition rather than a real plan." The e-commerce and cloud computing giant is building a competitor to SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service, and said it would take SpaceX "centuries" to build the constellation, adding that the company provided scant details about how it would "deliver on these grand claims." The petition resulted in a rebuke from Carr , who said Amazon "should focus on the fact" that it's falling short of its own satellite deployment milestone. Other companies have also set their sights on orbital data centers. Google last year announced Project Suncatcher , which it describes as a "moonshot to put AI in space," and launched its first chips into space on a SpaceX rocket and Planet Labs satellite in October. In March, Jeff Bezos ' Blue Origin petitioned the FCC to let it launch up to 51,600 satellites as part of a low Earth orbit satellite constellation dubbed "Project Sunrise." The constellation would work in tandem with Blue Origin's planned TeraWave satellite internet service, announced in January. Astrophysicist and author Adam Becker was critical of the FCC move in an email to CNBC on Wednesday. "Any serious attempt at this is going to further pollute the night sky and runs a serious risk of a cascading chain reaction of space junk collisions, which would be a disaster for all of humanity," he wrote. "Musk and Carr are either profoundly stupid themselves, or hoping the rest of us are too stupid to notice this is nonsense." The FCC said in its authorization that it dismissed "comments and concerns raised regarding topics over which the Commission has no authority, including environmental concerns," and concerns about its impact on "optical astronomy."

title: Nvidia leads tech sell-off as Huang comeback rally fizzles and AI concerns return
summary: Nvidia and other AI-linked stocks fell as investors weighed AI spending, inflation and higher-rate risks.
body: Technology stocks fell on Wednesday as excitement over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's return faded and failed to calm concerns over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence trade. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite declined 0.6% and traded off its lows, recovering from steeper losses earlier in the session. Semiconductor stocks dragged on the index, and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF that tracks the sector edged down 1%. "We just feel that this is panic right now," Venu Krishna, head of U.S. equity strategy at Barclays, told CNBC's " Squawk on the Street " on Wednesday. "What the market is telling you is that the AI growth narrative has hit a wall and given the centrality of that theme at the economic level, the market is expecting some sort of a macro shock," he added. After notching one of its best days on record Monday, Nvidia has fallen in the days since and slumped 4% Wednesday. Advanced Micro Devices , Marvell Technology and Intel all edged lower. Micron Technology declined 4%. Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday briefly revived appetite for tech stocks but didn't fully calm investor concerns over the high costs tied to the AI build-out and worries of a potential slowdown. Other stocks tied to the AI trade also plummeted. Oracle fell more than 5%. CoreWeave and Nebius moved lower. AI lab Anthropic bucked the sell-off, however, and climbed more than 4% after shares dropped below last week's blockbuster IPO price. Wednesday's declines also came as Wall Street digested a hot inflation reading that fueled concerns that higher interest rates could dent demand for growth stocks, including tech. Amazon and Alphabet each declined about 2%. Microsoft and Tesla lost more than 1% and Meta traded 3% higher.

title: There are 5,100 newly minted Anthropic millionaires—here’s all the stuff they don’t tell you about when you suddenly get rich
summary: Anthropic’s IPO made about 5,100 employees paper millionaires. Experts explain the risks of sudden wealth.
body: Things are about to get very weird for the thousands of employees of Anthropic who just became, or soon will become, multimillionaires. Anthropic's IPO on Nov. 19 turned around 5,100 nonfounder "Ants," as the company's staffers are known, into "paper millionaires," and at least 400 will be worth north of $100 million. Few of us will ever make a million-dollar windfall from an employer. And fewer still will win the lottery or magically land a massive sum from an estranged rich uncle. But don't be too jealous of these employees' gains. Sure, money can buy a lot — and it would be hard to say no if you do strike it rich — but there are a remarkable number of downsides to sudden wealth. And they may explain why you likely won't see all of Anthropic's newly minted millionaire employees heading for the exits. First of all, these new moguls won't be able to access all their wealth immediately. The terms of the stock sale outlined in Anthropic's revised S-1 allow employees to cash out up to 10% of the value of their holdings on the first day of trading following the date of the prospectus, but the rest can only be exercised after various vesting periods pass or lock-up terms are achieved, based on the individual's agreements with the company. Some won't be able to realize all their gains for years. There are many financial institutions willing to lend based on paper gains, or to buy options — but their wealth will also continue to fluctuate with the rise and fall of the company's stock price. Even after those riches become liquid, research shows that only a small but still significant percentage of employees will leave as a direct result of their new wealth. No, they aren't jetting off to the South Pacific to board their new yacht — which is what I would do in my "I just got $10 million" fantasy. Instead, according to a 2017 study from the Federal Reserve , an estimated 17.5% of employees at a newly public company will use their newfound wealth as a financial cushion to join another pre-IPO startup or form another company. These departures, the study finds, may be particularly painful for Anthropic since the most valuable and entrepreneurially minded employees tend to bolt for this reason. Experts who deal with suddenly wealthy employees expect that many will keep on working because they love it. "They're successful people in their own right," said David Rust, a financial advisor and co-founder of wealth management firm Quartz Financial in Austin, Texas. Rust said that of his firm's high-tech employee clients who get sudden IPO wealth, "very few just go play golf every day. They want to stay busy and active, and a lot of them will scale back depending on their age, but very few of them say, 'OK, I'm done with that.'" Others will keep working because their payout wasn't life-changing, said Susan Bradley, a certified financial planner and founder of The Sudden Money Institute, a Palm Beach Gardens, Florida-based financial advisory firm that specializes in clients undergoing sudden wealth events. That's especially true for those whose millions measure in the low single digits. "You can go through $2 million pretty quickly in the world we live in," said Bradley. A sum north of $1 million might seem life-changing to most of America, but it's chump change in Anthropic's headquarters city of San Francisco, the fifth most expensive city in the United States, with nearby San Jose coming in at third, according to a Q3 2026 Cost of Living report from Council on Community and Economic Research, which tracks metro- and state-level economic data. In 2025, the Bay Area had the second-highest number of people with a net worth of $100 million or more of any major metro in the world, according to a study by New World Wealth, a market research firm, in conjunction with Henley & Partners, a global residency and citizenship planning firm. title: Investors led by U.S. billionaire Todd Boehly to buy Lukoil's oil and gas assets outside Russia, sources say
summary: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation and Catena Investments, based in the United Arab Emirates, are also parties to the deal, the sources said.
body: Investors led by U.S. billionaire Todd Boehly's asset management company Eldridge have struck a deal to buy Lukoil's assets outside of Russia, sources confirmed to CNBC. The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation and Catena Investments, based in the United Arab Emirates, are also parties to the deal, the sources said. The deal transfers Lukoil's international refineries and other production assets in Bulgaria, Romania, Africa and the Middle East to the U.S.-led group, the sources said. It also includes retail gas stations in the U.S., Europe and Asia, they said. The U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control is expected to sign off on the deal but final approval is still needed, the sources said. The deal would give the U.S.-led group about 350,000 barrels per day of production. The agreement would allow Europe to buy fuel such as diesel previously produced by Lukoil through the U.S.-led group rather than Russia.

title: Kalshi traders say the odds of states imposing data center moratoriums is more likely than not
summary: After Democrats swept Congress and key governor races, Kalshi traders lowered the odds that at least four states would pause data center build-out this year.
body: On Wednesday morning, Kalshi traders put the probability above 55% that at least four states would adopt data center moratoriums this year. After Democrats swept Congress and key governor races during the midterm elections, Kalshi traders put the odds that at least four states would pause data center construction at about 75%. Since Nov. 22, the probability that at least four states would adopt moratoriums rose again, to 57% from 52%. The contract asks "How many states will adopt data center moratoriums this year?" and will be verified from state governments. On July 14, New York became the first state to impose a one-year pause on certain state permits for hyperscale data centers. Various local governments have also ordered moratoriums on data centers this year. Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., called for a national data center moratorium the day after the midterms on social media , signaling growing pushback against the build-out. Meanwhile, some investors say unease surrounding the artificial intelligence trade is partly an emotional or sentiment-driven reaction. Doug Clinton, founder and CEO of Intelligent Alpha, told CNBC's " Closing Bell: Overtime " the AI sell-off is psychological. "I actually think it is difficult to point to some fundamental data point from here that all of a sudden would make investors okay," Clinton said. AI-related stocks slumped again Wednesday. Nvidia and Oracle slid more than 8%, while Anthropic tumbled 6% and Alphabet slid 5.5%. On Friday, the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average entered corrections, down 10% from their recent highs, while the Nasdaq Composite declined more than 5% following Anthropic's blockbuster public offering the day before. The ones doing the predictions are citing the rebound in export flows out of the Persian Gulf, but they seem to be forgetting something. These export flows were up in September and October. Now, they’re down. The war is not over, and neither is the risk to global oil supply. One recent indication of that was the news that Chinese refiners, state-owned and independent, have ramped up their buying from abroad—and not only from the Middle East. Sinopec, for instance, has bought about 20 million barrels of crude since the start of this month from West Africa alone, for delivery next month. That is equivalent to all Chinese refiners’ West African oil purchases in a typical month. Yet purchases from the Middle East are also on the rise, the report, by Bloomberg, said, suggesting export rates are indeed normalizing. Except the number of tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz has gone significantly higher as well. Just at the beginning of this week, three tankers were damaged after they struck mines, although the UK Maritime Trade Operations said three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles. Mines and/or attacks on tankers have become a daily occurrence in the chokepoint—and daily traffic rates are down. Related: Iraq Refuses to Accept OPEC+ Assessment of its Production Capacity Indeed, tanker traffic in Hormuz was already down in early October, from the September rebound. That was according to Kpler, which has turned into the go-to source of tanker traffic information for all major outlets. It was Kpler analysts who said that by October 8, the number of tankers traversing the Strait of Hormuz had fallen to the lowest in two months, meaning July, to some 10.1 million barrels daily. “That is back to its September average, but 74% of its pre-war level,” the analysts noted at the time. This does not exactly match the glut story that some investment banks and the International Energy Agency are putting forward, and that has depressed prices and quite likely lulled oil traders into a false sense of security that all is back to normal in the Persian Gulf and a formal peace is only a matter of time—even as President Trump suggested to Fox News that the United States could restart its attacks on Iranian targets in 2027. The consortium will exchange Lukoil securities worth $10 billion for the assets. The securities were bought from US and British funds and from US depositary banks that held them for retail investors, according to a person familiar with the terms. Western investors' Lukoil shares were frozen after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022 and written down. "We're basically exchanging shares that are worthless to Americans ... for cash that is going back to them," said Boehly, chief executive of the asset manager Eldridge. The shares will be held in escrow in the UAE rather than going to Lukoil, the person said, to win approval from the Treasury Department, which has barred any windfall to the Russian company. Two people familiar with the terms valued the portfolio at about $16 billion. It covers operations in 11 countries producing around 350,000 barrels per day, including oilfields in Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan, refineries in the Netherlands, Bulgaria and Romania, and a network of service stations that includes some in the United States. In early November, Reuters reported that the assets were initially valued at $22 billion. Through the DFC, the US government will receive a share of future profits once the private investors recoup their capital and an agreed return, and it will have a role on the company's board. "Moving strategic energy infrastructure assets into US or allied partners' hands is a key policy priority of the administration," a DFC official said. The deal needs approval from the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), and Boehly said closing could take up to a year. The consortium now includes US bank Xtellus Partners and UAE-based Catena Investment Holding. Two partners left last week: the Syrian-Qatari Al-Khayyat brothers and Abu Dhabi's International Holding Company. Washington sanctioned Lukoil in October 2025, which forced the company to sell its foreign holdings. Two earlier buyers failed to close. Gunvor withdrew its offer after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the trader the "Kremlin's puppet." Lukoil then agreed in January to sell the assets to Carlyle , excluding its stakes in Kazakhstan's Karachaganak and Tengizchevroil projects and the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, but OFAC never licensed that deal. The request comes four days before the group meets to set its output policy for 2027. US consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is assessing capacity for every OPEC+ member except Russia, Iran and Venezuela. Kazakhstan's energy ministry confirmed the review had taken place but did not comment on its findings or next steps. Kazakhstan's OPEC+ quota for November and December is 1.628 million barrels per day, according to OPEC data . The International Energy Agency (IEA) estimated Kazakh crude output at 1.76 million bpd in October, about 8% above that target. Chevron began production from the $48 billion Future Growth Project at Kazakhstan's Tengiz field in January 2025. Export disruptions have also capped Kazakh output this year. The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), which carries more than 80% of Kazakhstan's oil exports to a terminal near Novorossiysk on Russia's Black Sea coast, suspended loadings in July after drone strikes on tankers at the terminal. Kazakh oil and condensate output fell about 21% to 1.63 million bpd from a July average of 2.07 million bpd, and production at Tengiz fell 56%. The IEA puts Iraq's sustainable capacity at 4.87 million bpd. Iraq has warned it may leave OPEC if its quota is not raised, according to Reuters. The challenges follow the UAE’s exit from OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1. Abu Dhabi had argued for years that its quota did not account for its investment in new capacity. Angola left OPEC in January 2024. title: Gold at $8,000 could signal dollar crisis: economist
summary: Alasdair Macleod warns that the Federal Reserve may have to sacrifice the currency’s purchasing power to protect markets.
body: Alasdair Macleod warns that the Federal Reserve may have to sacrifice the currency’s purchasing power to protect markets. Gold’s next rally could expose a sharp deterioration in the value of the US dollar, economist and financial commentator Alasdair Macleod says. Despite uncertainty over the timing of a rebound amid expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, Macleod sees the precious metal potentially reaching $8,000 per oz. within six months. “It doesn’t mean that gold has gone up,” Macleod told MINING.COM host Devan Murugan on the latest Top of Mine episode. “It means the dollar has gone down. And this is the point which I think everybody misses.” Macleod’s outlook challenges conventional investment thinking, particularly the tendency to view gold through the lens of interest rates rather than as a means of preserving wealth against currency depreciation. For him, investors need to better understand gold and what it means to hold it. “We live in this Keynesian world where the first reaction is you sell gold for whatever reason, like ‘rising interest rates is bad for gold because of the opportunity cost,’ or all this rubbish which actually just completely misunderstands what gold is,” he said. Macleod sees that the problem is in the American market, where investors own little gold while we are on the verge of an ‘uncomfortable’ bear market in equities. A liquidity squeeze, he argues, could prompt indiscriminate asset selling. “The basic message I have for everyone is the risk is in credit,” Macleod said. “Get out of credit, get into physical gold and be happy.” Macleod said that he wouldn’t want to be in the Fed’s position, as that choice to raise interest rates will decide what is protected: either the dollar or the financial system. “They will do whatever it takes to try and rescue the economy and rescue financial markets,” he said. “That becomes a priority, not protecting the dollar.” Central bank intervention to ease liquidity pressures could come at the expense of confidence in the currency, Macleod warns. “It’s their currency going down. And when people generally realize that, particularly the users of the currency, then the currency is finished.”

title: Copper price sinks to 2026 low as mining stocks brace for further losses
summary: In every copper bear market since 1970, prices gave back the vast majority of the bull market's gains, a new analysis shows.
body: In every copper bear market since 1970, prices gave back the vast majority of the bull market's gains, a new analysis shows. Copper fell to its lowest level this year on Wednesday, extending a selloff that has erased about $145 billion from the market value of the world’s biggest copper miners in November. Comex copper for December delivery fell 2.1% to $5.25 a pound ($11,584 a tonne) around midday in New York, after touching $5.222. That is below the March 20 settlement of $5.3425, the previous low for 2026, and a settlement at today’s level would be the lowest since early December last year. The red metal is now down 7% this year and almost 19% in November, and sits 24% below its record settlement of $6.889 on September 9. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell 1.9% to $11,596 a tonne in afternoon trading in London, its weakest since December 16. New York and London prices are now roughly level, after tariff bets kept Comex at a hefty premium for most of the past two years. History offers little comfort to copper bulls. Every bear market in copper since 1970 “has taken back the vast majority of each bull market’s gains,” John Gross wrote in The Copper Journal on Friday. He calls it the “Give Back”. In each of the 11 bull markets before this one, a 10% fall from the peak was followed by a 20% drop and a bear market, Gross found. Losses from the high ranged from 32% to 69% and averaged 49%. Comex copper crossed his 20% line, $5.44 a pound on his measure, this week. A 49% loss from September’s record would take Comex copper to about $3.50 a pound. Gross does not forecast the outcome of this cycle, and his study looks only at price behaviour, setting aside fundamentals and economics. Stocks have a better record: after a 10% fall, the S&P 500 has gone on to break through its 20% line only about half the time, he noted. New US tariffs and inflation data added to the pressure on Wednesday. The Trump administration proposed duties on 14 trading partners , including 20% on China, and figures released the same morning showed US inflation rose further in October, stoking worries about more interest rate hikes. Nvidia fell more than 8%, the Nasdaq Composite 3.5% and the S&P 500 2.4%. Copper itself is largely outside the new package. For 13 of the 14 economies, the proposed duties would not apply to goods already covered by Section 232 tariffs, including copper articles, according to law firm Baker McKenzie . The decision that matters most for the metal, a proposed 15% tariff on refined copper imports from 2027, remains unresolved . BMO Capital Markets expects the selloff to run until Washington signals its tariff intentions or prices fall far enough to hit supply, potentially in the $10,000 to $11,000 a tonne range, the bank said this week . Financial flows have overpowered a physical market where visible exchange stocks cover only about two days of consumption, BMO said, and traders have booked an estimated 30,000 to 100,000 tonnes of US copper for shipment to China, a sign they are losing faith in a tariff that would keep US stockpiles sealed off. The bank stands by its structurally bullish medium-term view. “People had been trying to get into the hard-assets trade and AI expansion and growth, but I think this unwrapping and unwinding has more to go,” George Griffiths, head of markets at AMT Futures, told Reuters. Open interest in copper has declined significantly, he said. title: Nine dead, 17 trapped after illegal gold mine floods in Indonesia
summary: Rescue crews pump water from a 100-metre shaft in West Java as difficult terrain and poor visibility hamper efforts.
body: Rescue crews pump water from a 100-metre shaft in West Java as difficult terrain and poor visibility hamper efforts. Rescue crews pumping water from flooded shaft. ( Image: Screenshot from Global News Network+ | YouTube. ) Indonesian rescuers are searching for miners trapped underground after heavy rains inundated an unauthorized gold mining operation in West Java province. The miners have been trapped since Monday in a 100-metre-deep shaft in the Pongkor area of Bogor, a mountainous region 60 km south of Jakarta. Authorities have been pumping water from the shaft to facilitate recovery efforts, the search and rescue agency said Wednesday. “The depth of the shaft, narrow access and limited lighting are key considerations in determining the search strategy so that personnel can operate safely,” Desiana Kartika Bahari, head of the Jakarta Search and Rescue Office, said according to local news outlet Detik . The disaster underscores the challenges Indonesia faces in regulating small-scale mining across its resource-rich but often remote regions, where informal operations provide precarious livelihoods for thousands of workers. State-owned miner Antam, which operates gold mines in Pongkor, said the incident occurred at an unauthorized site unrelated to its operations. “The problem was that nobody reported it and nobody wanted to report it because the activity was illegal,” said Muhammad Adam Hamdani, head of emergency and logistics at the Bogor disaster mitigation agency. The incident comes after authorities shut down about 30 gold mining pits in a separate area of Bogor last week. Workers at informal mining operations face persistent threats from landslides and tunnel collapses. Gold ore processing also frequently involves highly toxic substances such as mercury and cyanide, with miners often using little or no personal protective equipment.

title: ValOre seeks financing for $135M Brazil gold deal
summary: Água Azul would give ValOre a second Brazilian property, as well as a first operating asset.
body: Água Azul would give ValOre a second Brazilian property, as well as a first operating asset. View of ValOre's Pedra Branca property in Brazil. Credit: ValOre Metals. Canadian developer ValOre Metals (TSXV: VO; US-OTC: KVLQF) agreed to buy the Água Azul gold mine in Brazil for $135 million (C$193 million) — more than 20 times the company’s market value before trading was halted Tuesday. Vancouver-based ValOre plans to buy Bemisa Água Azul Mineração and an associated landholding entity from the Opportunity Holding investment fund, according to a statement Tuesday. The agreement will require a $90 million payment at closing, followed by $20 million after one year and $25 million after two years, subject to adjustments. ValOre, which still needs to secure acquisition funding, expects the deal to close by Jan. 15, subject to TSX Venture Exchange acceptance. “Advanced” financing discussions covering the purchase, working capital and initial development spending are ongoing, the company said. Under the agreement, ValOre has a one-time option within four months of closing to settle all $45 million of deferred payments for $30 million, subject to United States inflation adjustments. Exercising it would cut the nominal purchase price to $120 million. Located about 1,900 km northwest of Sao Paulo, Água Azul would give ValOre a second Brazilian property, as well as a first operating asset. The company is already developing the Pedra Branca platinum group elements project in Ceará state, about 200 km from Fortaleza. Água Azul includes a 206-sq.-km land package that hosts the Abelhas, Juliano and Campos Altos deposit areas along a 15-km structural trend. Its Abelhas open-pit gold mine feeds a plant processing about 120,000 tonnes of material a year. A preliminary economic assessment dated July 28 evaluates increasing the plant’s processing capacity to 2.85 million tonnes a year, following a three-year development period. The study estimates $297 million in initial capital, including plant expansion, pre-stripping and contingency. At a 5% discount rate and a long-term gold price of $3,609 per oz., it calculates an after-tax net present value of $927.6 million and a 48% internal rate of return. Água Azul’s mine schedule spans 13 years, including about a decade at the expanded capacity. Estimated all-in sustaining costs are $1,540 per ounce. The assessment is preliminary and includes inferred resources, which are too speculative to support mineral reserves. The property holds 22.8 million indicated tonnes grading 1.27 grams per tonne gold containing 931,920 oz. gold, according to a July 2026 resource. Inferred resources were estimated at 26.4 million tonnes grading 1.29 grams gold for contained metal of 1.1 million oz. gold. The acquisition comes as ValOre advances processing research at Pedra Branca. On Nov. 10, it announced a five-year cooperation agreement with Germany’s federal geoscience institute and mineral resources agency through the government-funded BioPlat research project. Shares of ValOre were halted Tuesday because the deal constitutes a fundamental acquisition under TSX Venture Exchange rules. They closed at 3.5¢ on Monday, valuing the company at C$8.9 million ($6.2 million).

Liesman: Why Greenspan could bet on productivity — and Warsh needs to hike
summary: Alan Greenspan famously held the line on interest rates because he believed in the productivity promise of the internet boom. Why can't Kevin Warsh do the same?
body: In a discussion on CNBC's Halftime Report Wednesday, the question came up: Why can't Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh hold the line on interest rates the way his icon Alan Greenspan did at the beginning of the dot-com era? Greenspan famously leaned against inflation hawks on his committee in 1995 and 1996, holding the line on interest rates amid strong growth, because he believed in the productivity promise of the internet revolution. It would be nice if Warsh could follow the same playbook amid the artificial intelligence build-out and keep rates steady until the productivity arrives. Unfortunately, a quick look at the numbers shows just how different the situation is for Warsh when it comes to inflation , the magnitude of the capital-investment boom and the monetary and fiscal stimulus boosting the economy. Bottom line: the Fed looks like it has to hike — and maybe substantially — to be anywhere close to the position where the Fed was in Greenspan's time at the dawn of a major technological revolution. It may be that the massive capex spending on AI will mean more productivity and less inflation down the road. But the front-end build-out is proving to be more inflationary, and more challenging, to a Fed already dealing with high inflation. In many ways, that's the opposite of what Greenspan had to handle.

title: November 2026: Oil market sentiment shifts back towards oversupply - PetrolPrices
body: At the start of 2026, market sentiment was firmly bearish, with expectations of a global supply surplus and many analysts forecasting that Brent crude would remain below $60/bbl throughout the year. The US and Israeli strikes on Iran, followed by the wider conflict in the Middle East, fundamentally changed that outlook, pushing crude prices above $113/bbl. However, as the conflict has progressed and supply flows have begun to recover, market sentiment is once again shifting towards oversupply. OPEC+ production reached 41.23 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, bringing output close to pre-conflict levels. This recovery in supply, combined with expectations of weaker demand, has increasingly weighed on crude markets. The International Energy Agency (IEA) expects the market to move into surplus as early as the current quarter, while Goldman Sachs forecasts that supply could exceed demand by approximately 2 million bpd as consumption weakens and Middle Eastern flows continue to improve. The shift in sentiment is also evident in investor positioning. ICE Commitment of Traders data showed that, in the week ending 17 November, speculators reduced their net bullish positions in Brent crude by almost 3.5%, taking them to their lowest level in more than ten months. Short positions have also increased, with volumes exceeding 142 million barrels, their highest level in four months. Meanwhile, major investment banks, including Morgan Stanley and JP Morgan, have highlighted the recent build-up in oil inventories as further evidence of a market moving towards surplus. Brent crude has fallen below $87/bbl, down more than 23% from $113.35/bbl at the end of October. The decline in crude has fed through into refined product markets, with wholesale diesel prices almost 20ppl lower than at the start of November and unleaded more than 16ppl lower. Some of these reductions have now reached the forecourt. The average UK unleaded price is almost 12ppl lower than at the beginning of the month. Diesel has fallen more slowly, with the national average currently just under 7ppl lower. The difference in the rate of reduction reflects the pricing dynamics seen during the earlier period of high prices. Retailers were reluctant to push diesel prices above £2 per litre, leaving retail-to-wholesale margins under pressure. As wholesale prices subsequently fell, these margins returned towards more normal levels, delaying the full pass-through of lower costs to motorists. However, the retail-to-wholesale spread for both grades is now above recent averages, suggesting there is further scope for pump prices to fall as we move into December. The pace of retail reductions has also accelerated throughout November, with the number of price cuts increasing each week. Whether this momentum can be sustained into the final month of the year remains uncertain. A continued decline in wholesale costs should support further reductions, although retailers may become more cautious if the rate of wholesale price falls begins to slow. The easing of fuel prices will be welcome news for motorists, retailers and businesses, as well as the government. Lower energy costs should help to moderate inflationary pressures, although the wider impact will depend on how long the decline in wholesale markets is sustained. One factor working against UK fuel buyers is the weakness of sterling against the US dollar. The GBP/USD exchange rate closed at 1.3018 on 23 November, its lowest level since 2 April 2025. Expectations of further US interest rate increases have supported the dollar, while ongoing geopolitical uncertainty has also encouraged demand for the US currency. A weaker pound increases the sterling cost of imported crude and refined products, partially offsetting the benefit of lower international prices. title: Oil prices rise after Houthis say they attacked Saudi refinery - CNBC
body: Crude oil prices rose on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi ‌Arabia's largest oil refinery and traders weighed Middle East supply disruptions against the prospect of a global market surplus. Brent crude futures rose 3.5% to close at $94.61 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures climbed 2% to settle at $83.68. Both benchmarks gained more ​than 2% on Tuesday. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Wednesday that they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and ​Riyadh's financial district. The refinery, Saudi Arabia's largest, is part of a complex that also serves as ⁠a major export terminal for Saudi crude. The Houthi statement triggered Wednesday's price rally, said PVM oil analyst Tamas Varga, citing a ​rising geopolitical risk premium. Traders are also likely to be covering short positions ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday, which could add ​to the momentum, Varga said. U.S. crude inventories rose by 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million barrels in the week ended November 20, data from Energy Information Administration showed. That compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 1.5 million-barrel rise. The build in crude stocks ​was mainly due to weaker crude exports while imports rose, said Bob Yawger, director of energy futures at Mizuho. Prices also drew ​support from uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies ahead of its November 29 meeting, especially with the United Arab Emirates no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies ‌and Iraq ⁠seeking higher oil output capacity, said Zhenqiang Seto, an oil research specialist at LSEG. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy. "Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next ​year's production quotas will be ​determined at the OPEC+ meeting, ⁠Ueno added. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said OPEC+ is set to complete a review by year end of member production capacities. Iraq and Kazakhstan were pressing OPEC+ to raise its estimate of their oil ​production capacity, said four people familiar with the matter, heightening tensions over a review that ​will help determine ⁠how much members can pump next year. In other supply news, Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has reopened. Flows were halted when a valve was closed by what the National Oil Corporation described as an unlawful group. Oil is again flowing into storage tanks at the Akakus facility ⁠in Zawiya, ​NOC said. In the Strait of Hormuz, a container ship was targeted and came to a ​stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the strait, Iran's Revolutionary Guards told state media.

body: LONDON, Nov 24 (Reuters) – Oil prices fell to three-month lows on Tuesday on signs of rising crude supply and a potential market surplus, though risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz persisted. Brent crude futures were down 75 cents, or 0.8%, at $88.62 a barrel by 0915 GMT, ​after hitting its lowest since August 27. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were 64 cents, ‌or 0.8%, lower at $79.53 a barrel, after falling to the weakest since August 10. “Oil prices are facing modest downward pressure from two sides: markets are pricing out some near-term geopolitical risk in the Middle East, while releases from strategic reserves are keeping supply relatively comfortable despite lower regional exports and stronger Chinese demand,” said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo. “Brent has largely lost any upward impetus in ‌recent ​days as supply conditions remain benign despite the continued closure of the ⁠Strait of Hormuz, and the market ⁠weighs the possibility of a future supply glut against persistent Middle East tensions and shipping disruptions.” However, Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS Bank, said prices risk going higher again depending on talks between the US and Iran and as both parties could test the other’s resolve in blockading the strait. Iran’s ​Revolutionary Guards navy said three “violating” oil tankers had caught fire after hitting naval mines in the strait on Monday, Iran’s Press TV reported. The United States is also investigating whether Iran was involved in cyberattacks on as ⁠many as 50 energy tankers, the Wall Street Journal reported, ⁠citing US officials and others familiar with the matter. Libya’s Sharara oil pipeline has reopened ​after an “unlawful group” closed a valve on the pipeline, and oil has begun to flow into storage tanks at ​the Akakus facility in Zawiya, the chairperson of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on ‌Monday. China and India are on track for record Russian oil imports this year, plugging a supply gap shortage caused by the Iran war, according to tanker data and industry sources. Temporary US waivers on Russian oil sanctions, aimed at keeping markets supplied amid the Middle East crisis, widened the pool of vessels and suppliers available to India ⁠and China, allowing them to increase purchases. While better supply is weighing on prices, analysts said the market remained fragile. “Oil prices, time spreads, refining margins and investor positioning increasingly suggest the market expects conditions to normalise,” Daniel Hynes, senior ⁠commodity strategist at ANZ, said in a ‌client note. “Yet logistics remain constrained and inventory buffers are thin.” Deutsche Bank said that ⁠global observed liquids’ inventory rose in October, implying an oversupply of 1.7 million ​barrels each ‌day. Evidence is accumulating that the global market is rebalancing and turning ​into surplus, although ⁠setbacks could delay progress, the bank said in a research report. US crude oil and product inventories likely rose last week, a preliminary Reuters poll showed. Elsewhere, Iraq’s prime minister has ordered the federal oil ministry to manage oilfields in areas under Kurdish security control, the state news agency said on Tuesday, potentially deepening tensions between Baghdad and the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region. body: Sessions framed around the Strait of Hormuz sit in a well-worn category: the waterway carries a large share of seaborne crude, and episodes of reported closure orders, mine strikes and tanker incidents have historically priced a geopolitical risk premium into prompt spreads and freight and insurance costs faster than into outright flat price, with the premium decaying quickly once physical flows prove uninterrupted. The tell in past episodes of this kind is whether disruption is confirmed in loadings and shipping fixtures rather than in headlines, since rhetoric alone has tended to fade within sessions. Inventory prints from the private survey have rarely sustained direction against a geopolitical driver and mainly set up positioning for the official data that follows. The divergence in the complex is familiar: crude bid on supply-risk, gold sidelined ahead of the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, copper tracking broader risk sentiment, which separates the supply-shock leg from the macro leg. Worth watching are confirmation or denial of the closure order, tanker traffic and insurance rates through the strait, and the PCE release as the next scheduled catalyst for the metals side.

body: Russian oil exports reached their highest level since 2022 this year. Analysts expect a global surplus and a possible drop in prices. The increase in oil supplies from Russia is contributing to the formation of a surplus of supply, which is expected to shape the state of the oil market next year and possibly in the years to come. Bloomberg reports, UNN writes. Russia’s exports have averaged 3.65 million barrels per day since the beginning of the year, the highest annual average since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. At the same time, according to tanker-shipment data compiled by Bloomberg, overseas supplies in the four weeks through November 22 fell slightly to 3.92 million barrels per day, 30,000 barrels per day below the revised figure for the period through November 15. The increase in exports adds to growing supplies from the Persian Gulf, prompting an increasing number of market analysts, including Goldman Sachs Group Inc., JPMorgan Chase & Co. and Sanford C Bernstein, to forecast a return to a global oil surplus, which could potentially lead to lower prices. The price of Brent crude has fallen by almost a quarter from its late-October high. On Sunday, oil ministers of OPEC+ countries, led by Russia and Saudi Arabia, are due to hold talks to establish preliminary production targets for 2027. These levels will be calculated on the basis of new baselines, using external assessments of each country’s sustainable production capacity. Russia’s exports have increased this year despite the country’s difficulties in raising production in line with the increase in OPEC+ targets. Strikes on refineries are forcing Moscow to redirect oil it cannot process to exports, increasing overseas oil sales. A lull in these strikes generally allows repair work to be carried out, increasing refining and returning oil to domestic refineries, the publication writes. title: Bank of Canada expected to hike interest rate next month, economists say - Global News
body: Some Canadians could see their finances tighten more as economists say they expect the Bank of Canada to increase its key interest rate again next month. The prediction comes after they say the central bank’s governor, Tiff Macklem, warned Tuesday that cost pressures are building on businesses. “We thought that there might be an opening where the Bank of Canada could delay the next interest rate increase into early next year,” said Sal Guatieri, BMO Capital Markets senior economist. “But that seemed to just go out the window with the governor basically just confirming that the bank is still quite concerned about energy costs pass-through to the broader measures of inflation.” Guatieri said Canadians could see at least a 0.25 basis point increase, bringing the key interest rate to 2.75 per cent. During his speech at the Economic Club of Canada, Macklem spoke of ongoing economic “shocks” and said that while oil prices and refinery margins have dropped, inflation is expected to persist. He also predicted a “second-round effect of the oil shock” will add to that in the new year. Guatieri added that with the governor still describing the economy as “resilient,” and its goal to get inflation under control, another hike is likely needed. The Bank of Canada is expected to deliver its next rate decision on Dec. 9 — its last of 2026. It announced a rate hike of 0.25 basis points on Oct. 28, bringing the policy rate to 2.5 per cent – the first time it had raised the rate in more than three years. At the time, Macklem said the decision was an effort to prevent higher energy prices from spreading to the prices of other goods and services. It was also seen as a response to pressure the bank faced due to the Iran war and other geopolitical conflicts resulting in higher prices for oil and gas. Macklem said Tuesday that when disruptions, such as to oil markets, push prices up without slowing economic growth, it can cause higher prices for households. When this happens, along with worse job prospects, the central bank has to weigh the risk of ongoing inflation with the possibility of weakening the economy with further interest rate changes. “The best contribution monetary policy can make to the well-being of Canadians is to keep inflation low, stable and predictable,” said Macklem. Though he stressed the economy was showing resilience, CIBC Chief Economist Avery Shenfeld said they’ve seen it weaken. “That still leaves us now thinking that he wants to raise interest rates sooner than later rather than wait and see another month or two,” Shenfeld said. With the potential for businesses that have shouldered the increased costs of transportation and production for some time to start passing those higher costs down to consumers, the bank is likely to take action again. According to Shenfeld though, December might be where the rate hikes stop – at least for now. “We don’t expect this inflation outburst to last too long, and we don’t expect to see a lot of interest rate hikes either,” he said. “We expect that December hike to be the last one we’ll see for quite a while.” Even if a rate hike is expected in an effort to battle back persistent inflation, Guatieri cautions the Bank of Canada from doing so. He said if the economy is weaker than expected, there’s a softer labour market and if unemployment continues to rise, interest rate hikes could have a heavier affect. That stands more true if a trade deal — even an interim one — isn’t reached with the U.S. and more tariffs come into effect in January. “It could end up being premature and who knows, the bank may end up having to reverse these rate increases if the economy softens through the next year,” Guatieri said.

title: S&P warns Nvidia credit rating could be cut over 'rising' management and governance risk
summary: S&P Global Ratings said Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch as it flagged "rising" management and governance risk at the chipmaker.
body: Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch over the next 90 days if the company continues to have "deficiencies" in its management and governance framework, S&P Global Ratings said in the wake of the Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as Nvidia CEO. "News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in Nvidia's management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness," S&P said in a Wednesday note . Nvidia currently holds an AA rating, the third-highest level. S&P has placed the chipmaker on "CreditWatch with negative implications," though any potential downgrade would be limited to one notch, to AA-, unless investigations or disclosures lead the agency to conclude that Nvidia's reputation or future prospects have also been harmed. A downgrade can pressure bond prices, push yields higher and raise borrowing costs. Nvidia priced $25 billion of investment-grade senior notes in June, with maturities from 2028 through 2056, shortly after S&P upgraded the company from AA- to AA. Nvidia has about $32.5 billion of bonds in the U.S. high-grade corporate bond index, according to Bloomberg. S&P's Wednesday note follows Moody's Ratings changing its outlook on Nvidia to stable from positive on Nov. 18, citing governance concerns, and leaving that outlook unchanged after Huang's return on Monday. In its note, S&P cited the "long tenure" of certain board members as a reason their independence may be "compromised" and said Nvidia's management and governance risk was "rising." The ratings agency added that it remained unaware of any remedial action taken by the board to address what could be "meaningful" management and governance deficiencies. Chairman Harvey Jones and early investor Tench Coxe have served on Nvidia's board since 1993, while Brooke Seawell joined in 1997. Mark Stevens served from 1993 to 2006 and rejoined the board in 2008. S&P also flagged questions around geopolitical risk management and internal controls arising from Nvidia's exposure to China. "While Nvidia management has delivered significant returns for its stakeholders over decades, weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning have brought questions around the "key man" risk to the forefront," S&P's Andrew Chang and David Tsui said. Chang and Tsui noted that Huang's resignation and subsequent reinstatement did not resolve questions about the board's oversight of executive conduct. The agency also intends to meet with Nvidia's board and management to discuss plans to address those deficiencies, particularly around "board independence, effective management oversight and a credible leadership succession plan." Huang returned less than two weeks after Jones said Nvidia's directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back, sending Nvidia shares up as much as 36% during Monday's session.

body: The surprise is large, but the market reaction is likely to stay muted because so much of the spending is imported equipment that does little for local output or wages. Investors are more likely to focus on what it says about capacity pressure and the RBA's December decision, where any lift in hike odds would support the Australian dollar and push up short-term yields. The industry mix matters for equities: the boom is concentrated in data centres and technology rather than mining, which favours data centre operators, construction and electrical contractors, and power suppliers over the resources sector that dominated past investment cycles. Australia's investment boom is back near mining-boom highs, but this time it's being built from server racks rather than iron ore mines. Australian business investment surged far beyond expectations in the third quarter. Private capital spending jumped 12.2% from the previous quarter, almost three times the 4.4% rise economists had forecast, Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed on Thursday. The figures, released at 0030 GMT (1930 US Eastern on Wednesday), put total capex at about A$59.5 billion for the quarter in inflation-adjusted terms, 18.6% higher than a year earlier. That takes it close to the peak reached during the mining investment boom more than a decade ago. The jump came almost entirely from equipment. Spending on plant and machinery soared 23.1% in the quarter and 34.3% from a year earlier, reversing an 8.9% fall in the June quarter and lifting it to a record. Investment in buildings and structures rose a more modest 1.7%. The industry detail points clearly to data centres. Total investment in information media and telecommunications, the industry that includes data centres, rose 86.7% in the quarter, and its equipment spending nearly tripled, up 183.5%. Earlier this year the ABS attributed a 6.5% jump in March-quarter capex to data centre equipment such as server racks and processing gear, and the June-quarter fall was widely seen as payback. Mining investment rose just 1.4%, while non-mining capex climbed 16.0%. Victoria led the states with a 31.0% rise. Firms also plan to keep spending. Their fourth estimate of capital expenditure for the 2026-27 financial year came in at about A$224 billion, 11.8% above the previous estimate. Planned equipment spending was revised up 20.4% to about A$102 billion, far outpacing a 5.6% upgrade for buildings and structures. There is an important caveat. Much of that equipment is imported , so a large share of the spending flows offshore rather than adding to domestic output. The boost to Australia's GDP will therefore be considerably smaller than the headline suggests. The ABS also completed its annual seasonal review with this release, which caused minor revisions to the equipment series. For the Reserve Bank of Australia, the data still adds to the case that the economy is running hot. The RBA raised its cash rate to 4.85% on November 3, its highest since 2008 and its fifth hike of the year, in a split 6-3 vote. The board said inflation remains broad-based and likely to stay above 3% for longer than previously expected, but it dropped its explicit warning about further increases. The RBA's final meeting of the year concludes on December 8, with the decision due at 0330 GMT (2230 US Eastern on December 7). October inflation data and third-quarter GDP figures will carry more weight before then, but strong investment intentions make it harder for the board to argue that demand is cooling. The figures also stand out against a global backdrop of growing resistance to data centre projects , from Tokyo's suburbs to Australia's own Northern Territory. title: U.S. Core PCE Inflation Hits 3.3%, Fed Seen Raising Rates in December and January - Businesskorea
body: With inflationary pressures in the United States remaining elevated, the Federal Reserve (Fed) is expected to raise interest rates in January, following a hike in December, according to an outlook from an iM Securities economist. In a report issued on Nov. 26, Park Sang-hyun, an economist at iM Securities, highlighted the 3.8% year-on-year increase in the U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index in October. The index also rose 0.3% from the previous month. Of particular note, the core PCE price index, which excludes food and energy and is closely watched by the Fed in setting monetary policy, increased 3.3% year on year, exceeding the market consensus of 3.2%. This marked its highest level since November 2023, underscoring persistent inflationary pressures. The so-called supercore PCE, which measures services prices excluding housing and energy, also rose 3.6%, indicating that inflationary pressures in the services sector remained elevated. Park said the inflation trend had effectively cemented the case for a Fed rate hike in December. He forecast that the Fed would raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a range of 4.00% to 4.25% in December, followed by another 25-basis-point increase in January, bringing the range to 4.25% to 4.50%. CME FedWatch, as cited in the report, also pointed to a 98.1% probability of a December hike and a 59.7% chance of a January increase at the time. However, the probability of another hike in March stood at 36.5%, suggesting that the policy path beyond January remained uncertain. Despite elevated inflation and interest rates, U.S. corporate investment has remained stronger than expected. The U.S. economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, revised upward by 0.9 percentage points from the initial estimate of 3.4%. This was the fastest pace of growth since the third quarter of 2023. Nonresidential fixed investment, a measure of business spending, surged at an annualized rate of 16%, contributing 2.22 percentage points to overall GDP growth. Orders for nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft also rose 1.2% month on month in October, well above the market forecast of 0.7%. The increase suggests that corporate investment plans remain solid. The recent sharp decline in AI- and semiconductor-related stocks could also become a factor in the Fed's monetary policy decisions. Park said equity markets were pressuring the Fed to avoid excessive tightening, adding that the central bank would find it difficult to ignore such market signals entirely. Whether the rate-hiking cycle continues beyond January, however, will depend on inflation data released in the coming months. The outlook for asset markets will depend largely on the interaction between inflation and investment trends. If inflationary pressures ease as oil prices stabilize at lower levels while the investment cycle remains resilient, asset prices, including equities, could stage a strong rebound. Conversely, if inflation remains elevated while investment momentum weakens, concerns over an economic slowdown or recession could weigh on financial markets. Park expects inflationary pressures to ease gradually, given the prospect of lower and more stable oil prices. He also believes the investment cycle will remain resilient despite recent concerns, leaving open the possibility of an earlier-than-expected rebound in the stock market.

Price increases also appeared across goods and services. Core goods prices rose 0.35% month over month, nearly doubling their previous pace, while their annual inflation rate increased to 2.3% from 2%. An economy capable of continuing to expand may still experience price pressures that require a restrictive policy setting, while changes in labour conditions can alter the balance of risks. Inflation measures changes in the general price level rather than an individual product's price. Particular items may become more expensive because of supply conditions, demand or changes in production and distribution costs. The policy question concerns the extent to which such movements contribute to persistent broader inflation. Williams identified inflation remaining too high relative to the Federal Reserve's price stability objective. Returning inflation sustainably to the desired level is distinct from recording a favourable result in a single reporting period. Policymakers consider a range of measures to assess the composition of price pressures. This can help identify whether changes are concentrated in particular categories or are becoming more widespread throughout the economy. The policy objective relates to the rate at which the general price level changes, rather than a requirement to reverse every increase in individual prices. A decline in inflation can therefore coexist with a price level that remains higher than it was earlier. That distinction matters when interpreting Williams's assessment. The persistence of inflation above the central bank's objective is relevant to the stance of monetary policy even when some individual categories have experienced periods of more moderate price growth. title: Fed’s Inflation Gauge Hits 3.8% as Strong Growth Adds Pressure for December Rate Hike - Business Times
body: US inflation accelerated in October as the Federal Reserve's preferred price gauge rose 3.8% from a year earlier, while stronger economic growth reinforced expectations of a December interest-rate increase and complicated the central bank's outlook for 2027. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased from September's 3.7% annual rate, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed to 3.3% from 3.1%, reaching its highest level since November 2023. The headline reading matched the Dow Jones consensus forecast, while core inflation exceeded expectations by 0.1 percentage point, CNBC reported. Both measures increased 0.3% from the previous month. Markets continued to fully price in a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting. Inflation has remained above the central bank's 2% target for roughly five and a half years. "Inflation is too hot and it will not be brought under control as long as economic demand is also too hot," said Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. A separate Commerce Department release showed gross domestic product expanded at a revised 4.3% annualized pace in the third quarter. Upward revisions to investment, consumer spending and government expenditures strengthened the picture of an economy maintaining substantial momentum despite tighter monetary policy. Consumer spending grew 4.2% during the quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure Fed officials monitor for underlying demand, increased 5.8%, an upward revision of 0.9 percentage point. October household spending offered a more subdued signal. Nominal expenditures rose 0.3%, slightly below expectations, while inflation-adjusted spending was essentially unchanged. Personal income increased 0.7%, exceeding the 0.4% forecast. The Bureau of Economic Analysis attributed the gain primarily to compensation, government social benefits and asset income, with one-time Medicare Improvement Fund premium rebates contributing to the increase in benefits. Disposable income rose 0.8% before inflation and 0.5% after adjusting for prices. With income outpacing spending, the personal saving rate increased to 4.1% from September's revised 3.6%. Stock-index futures extended losses after the releases, while Treasury yields fell sharply. Expectations for 2027 rate increases nevertheless eased somewhat: traders still priced in two hikes but reduced the probability of a third to approximately one-third from about 50% Tuesday, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The inflation figures arrive as policymakers assess pressures from the Iran war, tariffs and demand associated with artificial intelligence investment. The White House announced additional tariffs Wednesday covering 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union and Japan. While tariffs and supply disruptions can produce temporary price increases, some policymakers worry their effects could spread and become persistent. "America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. Labor-market data also showed continued resilience. Initial unemployment claims fell 13,000 to 189,000 in the week ended Nov. 21, below the 200,000 forecast and near their lowest levels since the late 1960s, the Labor Department reported.

Another big fund manager is making room for Hyperliquid, but the amount involved is tiny and the token's price is going the other way. Franklin Templeton's Franklin Crypto Index ETF (EZPZ) will start holding Hyperliquid's HYPE token on or around December 1, according to a prospectus supplement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 25. HYPE will be the only new name in the fund's lineup, taking it to eight assets alongside bitcoin, ether, XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, Cardano and Stellar. The change follows a November 16 notice from CF Benchmarks naming HYPE as the sole new constituent of its Institutional Digital Asset Index, which EZPZ tracks. The fund holds each asset at roughly its index weight and rebalances quarterly, so buying HYPE is an automatic index step, not a decision by Franklin. The filing does not disclose HYPE's starting weight. Scale matters here. EZPZ had about $17.02 million in net assets at the end of September, with bitcoin making up around 76% of the portfolio and ether close to 13%, according to fund data cited by crypto.news. As a rough illustration, a weight similar to the 3.36% HYPE received in Hashdex's Nasdaq CME Crypto Index ETF (NCIQ) in September would amount to only around $600,000 of the token. The addition shows where index products are heading. It won't add meaningful demand. Index adoption is spreading. Hashdex added HYPE to NCIQ from September 1, and the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index ETF added it in July. Three US spot HYPE ETFs launched this year now hold under $250 million in assets between them, The Block reported. Cumulative inflows into HYPE ETFs have topped $259 million despite a recent stretch of outflows. The price has not kept pace with the institutional interest. HYPE traded around $60 on November 25, well below the roughly $83 it fetched when Hashdex's inclusion was announced in late August. Even so, The Block reports the token is still up more than 120% on the year and ranks among the 10 largest cryptocurrencies, with a market value of about $13.6 billion. Regulation is the bigger thread. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said on November 19 that onchain platforms like Hyperliquid can reach US retail users either by partnering with an existing exchange or by obtaining their own. Payward, Kraken's parent company, is already pursuing a partnership route for decentralized derivatives venues. The next things to watch are HYPE's disclosed weight once EZPZ rebalances, whether flows into the dedicated HYPE ETFs turn positive again, and any concrete step by Hyperliquid toward a licensed US channel. title: US Inflation Climbs to 3.8% as Fed Faces Rate Decision - cwibc.co.id
body: Rising consumer prices are creating a tougher policy challenge for the Federal Reserve as US inflation accelerated in October, reaching nearly twice the central bank's 2% target. The Commerce Department reported the increase on Wednesday, raising concerns about further interest rate adjustments and the inflation outlook for 2027. The personal consumption expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure, increased at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.8%. That matched the Dow Jones consensus forecast but represented a 0.1 percentage point increase from September. Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, reached 3.3%, according to the Commerce Department. The figure exceeded economists' expectations by 0.1 percentage point. Although policymakers officially follow headline PCE, they consider the core measure a more reliable indicator of longer-term inflation trends. Separate economic data showed that US gross domestic product expanded at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, based on a revised Commerce Department estimate. The upward revision reflected stronger investment, consumer spending and government expenditure. Consumer spending, which represents approximately two-thirds of economic activity, increased 4.2% during the third quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure closely monitored by Federal Reserve officials as an indicator of underlying demand, climbed 5.8%, following an upward revision of 0.9 percentage point. Monthly consumer spending increased 0.3%, matching the pace of price increases but falling 0.1 percentage point short of forecasts. Personal income rose 0.7%, exceeding the 0.4% estimate, while the personal saving rate reached 4.1%. Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds, highlighted the relationship between economic demand and persistent price pressures. "Inflation is too hot and it will not be brought under control as long as economic demand is also too hot," said Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. Inflation pressures have been reinforced by several factors, including tariffs, energy costs and strong demand associated with the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure. The late-February attacks on Iran led by the US and Israel also preceded a renewed increase in inflation. The White House announced another round of tariffs on Wednesday covering 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union and Japan. While policymakers generally regard supply disruptions and tariffs as temporary pressures, concerns have grown that their effects could spread across the broader economy. Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said inflationary pressures extend beyond energy market disruptions. "America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. Financial markets showed mixed reactions following the economic releases. Stock futures extended their losses, while Treasury yields also moved sharply lower. Market expectations for additional Federal Reserve rate increases in 2027 eased slightly, although two further increases remained priced in. Expectations for a third increase fell to approximately one in three, compared with an even chance on Tuesday. Markets had fully priced in a 0.25 percentage point interest rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December 8-9 meeting. The larger question remains how much additional tightening policymakers may need to bring inflation back to their 2% target. Inflation has remained above that objective for approximately 5.5 years. Meanwhile, the Labor Department reported that initial unemployment claims declined to 189,000 for the week ending November 21. That represented a decrease of 13,000 from the previous week and was close to the lowest level recorded since the late 1960s. Economists had expected 200,000 claims.

Goldman Sachs forecasts that revenue will jump from roughly $52 billion in 2026 to $136 billion in 2027, an increase of more than 161%. Needham’s own model is for growth of 156%. “The history of the world’s never seen growth like this before at this scale,” Berg told Fortune , calling Anthropic the “leader in frontier intelligence.” Berg isn’t alone in his view. On Monday, Wedbush also issued a buy call with a $120 price target. Analysts called the stock in a note to clients “the clearest public way to own frontier AI at the start of a very large adoption curve.” The firm added that “the addressable market is vast, spanning a meaningful share of global knowledge work, and enterprise adoption is still early.” Canaccord Genuity initiated coverage Tuesday with a buy rating and a $135 target, pointing to Anthropic’s potential to become “one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era.” With all of this bullish commentary, why is the stock falling? Nvidia’s Monday rally, sparked by Jensen Huang’s return as CEO , faded on Tuesday as the Nasdaq Composite closed down nearly 1.5%. “I don’t think that short term volatility is unexpected given what we’ve seen,” Evan Schlossman, a principal at investment firm Neostellar Capital, told Fortune . Some experts predict Anthropic could pan out like Facebook’s 2012 IPO . That was roughly 54% below the IPO price. The stock didn’t climb back above $38 until the summer of 2013, after the company proved it could make money from mobile ads. title: Nvidia Gets Three Analyst Upgrades After Jensen Huang’s Return: Here’s Why CRWD, LI, DKNG, AMBA Made The List - Stocktwits
body: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) quickly won back Wall Street bulls after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, while CrowdStrike (CRWD) received two ‘Buy’ upgrades this week. Ambarella (AMBA), DraftKings (DKNG) and Insmed (INSM) drew downgrades, and Li Auto (LI) got a rare, welcome lift from JPMorgan after a third-quarter beat. Eleven days ago, analysts were bracing for the worst. Now, with Huang back as President, CEO and board member, the firms that stepped aside are stepping back in. Bernstein upgraded Nvidia stock to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Market Perform’ and left its price target at $200. The firm had downgraded the stock when Huang's conduct looked likely to cost him his job, and it cut its target in half. The exit came the next day. Huang's departure was the main reason for the downgrade, the analyst said, so his return undoes it. Bernstein still stays positive on the AI buildout. Valuation with Huang at the helm "seems supportive enough to us for now," said the analyst. Oppenheimer's Rick Schafer upgraded the stock to “Outperform” from “Perform” with a $250 target. He called Huang's return a "win for AI and a win for investors" and said it lifts a "major cloud of uncertainty." StoneX went furthest, upgrading to “Buy” from “Hold” with a $270 target. The firm said Huang’s return addresses five issues: the pace of the roadmap, industry relationships, willingness to back the AI buildout, organizational structure and the likely retention of key talent. Guggenheim upgraded CrowdStrike stock to “Buy” from “Neutral” with a $280 target, implying 33% upside. The firm expects "hyper growth and profit." The analyst noted that CrowdStrike works closely with every hyperscaler, even Microsoft, which some investors not long ago saw as a threat to the company's survival. Deutsche Bank's Brad Zelnick also upgraded CRWD to “Buy” from “Hold”, raising his target to $300 from $240. His argument is that the market hasn't fully priced in how much AI will expand the cybersecurity opportunity. He calls CrowdStrike the leader in the space and thinks its $565 billion total addressable market estimate for 2034 will prove conservative given the "tsunami of cyber demand materializing as the AI frontier advances." JPMorgan's Nick Lai upgraded Li Auto to “Neutral” from “Underweight” and nudged his target to $10 from $9. The catalyst was "a clean beat" in Q3, driven mostly by a better product mix and cost efficiency. The firm still expects a cautious industry backdrop into 2027 to weigh on profit. On Wednesday, Li posted its first earnings beat in three quarters . BofA cut Ambarella stock’s rating to “Underperform” from “Neutral” and slashed its target to $30 from $70. Q3 results landed at the low end of guidance, and Q4 outlook came in below consensus. The analyst thinks investors will struggle to underwrite a growth inflection with memory allocation uncertain and AI memory demand strong. DraftKings stock lost an “Overweight” at Morgan Stanley, where Stephen Grambling moved it to “Equal Weight” and lowered his target to $23 from $31. The multiple has compressed and estimates have fallen, he said, because marketing costs are higher again. He argued that visibility and risk-adjusted returns both erode as the company ramps its prediction markets investment. Insmed stock drew two downgrades from Truist and BMO Capital, both tied to Sanofi's (SNY) deal to acquire the company for $175 per share, a roughly $41 billion transaction. title: MU, SNDK, SKHY Jump As Nvidia Tests Kioxia Memory Fix — Analyst Presses Memory Giants For ‘Massive’ Buybacks - TradingView
body: Shares of Micron (MU), SanDisk (SNDK) and SK hynix (SKHY) jumped overnight heading into Thursday after Kioxia said its flash drives could help Nvidia ’s AI chips access a database of up to 2 trillion vectors. For ‘The Nvidia Way’ author Tae Kim, the question is how much confidence memory chipmakers have in their own long-term forecasts. He urged them to show it with “massive stock buybacks.” SNDK led the gains overnight, rising 4%, followed by SKHY up nearly 3%, MU up over 2%, and NVDA up over 1%. In Tokyo, Kioxia Holdings shares climbed nearly 15% to 7,895 yen on Thursday. A day earlier, the company said its operating unit would pay it 2.21 trillion yen on Friday. The cash stays within the Kioxia group. Shareholders will receive a separate payout on Dec. 8, when Kioxia pays its first interim dividend. Nvidia’s (NVDA) GB200 NVL72 rack pairs 72 GPUs with 13.4 terabytes of high-bandwidth memory (HBM). When an AI database exceeds capacity, the system may have to process it in batches and repeatedly move data between storage and memory. Nvidia’s SCADA software lets the GPUs retrieve small blocks of data directly from solid-state drives. For the test, Kioxia equipped one rack with 144 XD8 drives, adding about 1.1 petabytes of raw flash storage, which is 80 times the capacity of the rack’s high-bandwidth memory. Kioxia estimates that the setup could support a database of up to 2 trillion 512-byte vectors, the numerical representations AI systems use to find related information. The companies are still evaluating how efficiently the rack can process data at that scale. “The intelligence of AI agents will increasingly depend on the knowledge they can access, not just the compute power they consume,” said Jason Hardy, Nvidia’s vice president of storage tech. Kioxia also reported results for its next-gen GP2 drive. In a separate test, it handled more than 18 million random reads per second using 512-byte blocks, nearly twice its predecessor’s rate. Kioxia expects to send evaluation samples to select customers by the end of 2027. Kim urged memory chipmakers to back their forecasts by buying their own shares. For Micron, he pointed to Dec. 9. “Otherwise, all the talk about a strong multi-year outlook is just empty words. Show the market through actions,” he said on X. Dec. 9 is when Micron can start using its $35.16 billion buyback authorization under its U.S. CHIPS Act funding agreements. Last month, the board added about $33 billion to the $2.16 billion left under an earlier authorization, based on the company’s quarterly cash flow. Micron can decide how much of that amount to spend. For comparison, it spent $650 million repurchasing 2.5 million shares in all of fiscal 2026. On the other hand, SanDisk spent $5 billion buying back shares in the quarter ended Oct. 2 and still had $10.5 billion available for further purchases. SK hynix, meanwhile, plans to buy back and retire at least 60 trillion won worth of its shares as part of its fiscal 2026 shareholder returns. Data centers are becoming a bigger business for SanDisk , which makes flash memory with Kioxia. In its latest quarter, SanDisk’s data-center revenue rose 61% from the previous quarter to $4.8 billion, while consumer revenue fell 29% to $397 million. The partners are planning for the shift. In August, they outlined plans to invest more than $31 billion in Japan through 2032, contingent on government support. SK hynix could soon become Kioxia’s largest shareholder. It said last week that a bond conversion and share purchase would give it an indirect stake of about 14%. Micron, meanwhile, is already selling drives for AI workloads. In September, it said customers were receiving two lines of SSDs for systems that reuse earlier calculations to speed up AI responses. For investors, the question is how quickly those new uses translate into orders.
